cases.reviewerAnswer: Identify the referent and descriptive meaning of a familiar short noun phrase.
Muy precedes the adjective and remains invariant: muy grande, muy bonita, muy pequeños.
Alto means tall or high; the agreement forms are alta, altos and altas.
Azul means blue; its plural is azules, with no gender distinction.
Bajo means low or short in height; the agreement forms are baja, bajos and bajas.
Blanco means white; the agreement forms are blanca, blancos and blancas.
Bonito means pretty or nice; the agreement forms are bonita, bonitos and bonitas.
Grande means big or large; its plural is grandes, with no gender distinction.
Inteligente means intelligent; its plural is inteligentes, with no gender distinction.
Interesante means interesting; its plural is interesantes, with no gender distinction.
Muy means very and is invariant.
Negro means black; the agreement forms are negra, negros and negras.
Nuevo means new; the agreement forms are nueva, nuevos and nuevas.
Pequeño means small; the agreement forms are pequeña, pequeños and pequeñas.
Rojo means red; the agreement forms are roja, rojos and rojas.
Simpático means pleasant or likable; the agreement forms are simpática, simpáticos and simpáticas.
Verde means green; its plural is verdes, with no gender distinction.
Viejo means old; the agreement forms are vieja, viejos and viejas.
The lesson should teach gender and number agreement, selected gender-invariant adjectives, usual postnominal position, invariant muy and short-description comprehension.
